cards.flavor: Four generations on the same strip and Clover on the end of the row with a watering can too big for them, and somebody smaller still holding the other handle.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Market Gardener
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover completes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Saturday stall is not about the stall. It is about the seed money for the two identical beds Clover is going to plant differently on purpose.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Community Gardener
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy. If one does, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Clover turned the meadow behind the ward rooms into forty strips and handed thirty-nine of them away. Half the borough's gardeners started as the friend Clover brought along.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Rocket Botanist
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Potatoes will grow anywhere, they say, if you ask them nicely. There is a photograph of this in the Lending Library, and somebody else is in the doorway of it.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Master Botanist
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy. If one does, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every garden in three boroughs owes something to a cutting Clover once gave away, and every one of them was handed over with the same question: who else is coming?

cards.name: Clover’s Potato Experiment
cards.text: Requires Clover and an Agriculture Character. Gain 3 Supply, then you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Two identical beds, planted differently on purpose, exactly the way Clover's grandmother said was fussing. Hypothesis: potatoes. Conclusion: a great many more potatoes than expected, and somebody new holding the other end of the sack.

cards.name: Clover's Seed Drive
cards.text: Requires Clover. Gain 2 Supply, and another Agriculture Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Clover hands out packets on the strip all morning and will not take anything for them. Every one comes back as a basket in the autumn, and most of them come back with the gardener attached.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Rocket Mechanic
cards.text: When Comet completes a shift, the next Building you buy costs 1 less.
cards.flavor: She took the Crafts hall's engine course twice because she did not think she had understood it the first time. She had. She has never met a machine she did not want to sit inside.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Test Pilot
cards.text: Upgrades Comet. When Comet becomes upright, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck. Busy, once per game: Comet readies herself.
cards.flavor: The board turned her down twice. Both times she went away, learned the part they had marked her down on until she knew it better than they did, and came back. The test was: does it go up.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Astronaut
cards.text: Upgrades Comet. When Comet becomes upright, look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and gain 1 Supply. Busy, once per game: Comet readies herself.
cards.flavor: She got the seat on the third application and fell over on the way to the launch. She went anyway. From up here the Capital City is a very small market with very small bidding, and she has already read its order book.

cards.name: One Small Step
cards.text: Requires Comet and a Science Character. Gain 5 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: One small step for a Cat, taken on the third application by an animal who had already fallen over twice that morning. One enormous mess in the Crafts hall.

cards.name: Comet’s Countdown
cards.text: Requires Comet. Limited 3: at the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Three. Two. One. (Comet is still doing up her boots. She knows the sequence better than the board does; it is the boots that have never once gone to plan.)

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Penny Counter
cards.text: Busy, once per game: Copper readies himself.
cards.flavor: Counts the till twice and sleeps in it once. The second count is never about the till; it is about something he meant to put away and did not.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Scale Polisher
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. When Copper is recruited, the next Character you recruit costs 1 less.
cards.flavor: An honest measure makes a lasting friendship, and a lasting friendship makes a better price. Copper has never seen any tension between those two things.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Weights Inspector
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The merchants who used to lean on his scales learned to stop. Whatever comes for your Supply next, Copper had already worked out what it would cost and put that much aside.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Arcade Merchant
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. The first purchase you announce each turn may be announced for 1 less.
cards.flavor: He names a figure so mildly that the arcade takes a moment to notice it was a figure, and by then he has moved on to the weather.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Market Steward
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. At the start of your turn, the next Character you recruit costs 1 less. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The year the bridge went, they came and asked him to open the shelf. He said not yet. He said there will be worse. He lent them the salt on the quiet and the shelf is still shut.

cards.name: Dylan
cards.title: River Otter
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes back to the river after three of your turns. When Dylan is recruited, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another.
cards.flavor: He has held the licence since he was absurdly young and will not tell you how. He will tell you a story about how, and it is a very good story, and it is different every time.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Herb Gatherer
cards.text: When Rosabeth completes a shift, rehiring a Character from your Unemployment costs 1 less until your next turn.
cards.flavor: A basket twice her size, mint and thyme and something she will not name, and a song the whole row seems to know the end of.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Tincture Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. When Rosabeth is recruited, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: The Science hall has been through her notes twice and come away with a list of ingredients and no method. She is entirely relaxed about this. The method, she says, is the singing.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Apothecary
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: She closes the shop by putting every jar back where the jar wants to be, which takes a while, and she has never once thrown a recipe away.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Herbalist Physician
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. When Rosabeth becomes upright, you may rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for free, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Half the Hiring Hall's second chances started at her gate with a mug of something and an afternoon on the beds. She charges for the tincture and never for the rest of it, and she sends them back to the ground they came off.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Forager
cards.text: When Bella is recruited, your next Event needs one fewer Character. If you control no Buildings, gain 2 Supply as well.
cards.flavor: She was seven, the basket was bigger than she was, and she carried it home full in the week the grange had told everybody there was nothing out there.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Field Scientist
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. When Bella completes a shift, draw 1 card, and gain 1 Supply as well if you control one Building or none.
cards.flavor: Three notebooks and the recorder, because by the time she has found the right notebook the bird has gone and she is talking to herself about it anyway.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Field Recorder
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to the bottom of your deck.
cards.flavor: Fifteen years of the same square of hedgerow, every visit dated, and she will tell you without looking it up which year the frost came early.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Wildlife Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: The warden's badge changed nothing about her day. She still sits down in the dirt; she just has the authority to tell somebody else to.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Ecologist
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Your first Event each turn needs one fewer Character, and while you control three Buildings or fewer the first Event you play each turn also gives you 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Science hall cites her now, which she finds funny, because the finding they cite is that the wood was doing all of this perfectly well before any of us turned up with a shovel.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Auctioneer's Boy
cards.text: Busy: you may raise one of your open bids by 1.
cards.flavor: Nine years old, not allowed to bid, and already the only animal in the room who knew what everything in it was worth.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Peddler
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. When you announce a purchase, add 1 Supply to it and look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: The clocks were the high point. Six of them, same household, four years, and they still buy their flour off him.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Fair Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning. When a bid is tied, add 1 Supply to yours.
cards.flavor: He keeps the fair honest, which mostly means keeping an eye out for the Finn of five years ago. He knows exactly where that animal would be standing, and exactly what he would do about a tie.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Trade Broker
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. Whenever you gain a non-Statue Capital City card, gain 1 Supply. When you announce a purchase, look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: His percentage is small and he takes it off everything, and he knows what is coming up before the animal selling it does. The committee that reappointed him last spring knows precisely that, and reappointed him anyway.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Barrow Hand
cards.text: When Hazel completes a shift, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: One barrow, no stall, and a route round the bins that took all night and turned up something worth having every single time.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Night Market Vendor
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Recruit: draw 1 card, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: Everything half price after dark, on the stated grounds that you cannot quite see it and the unstated grounds that Hazel already knows which one you will take.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Market Vendor
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Busy: look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The bottles have no labels and the keys fit no door anyone can name, and Hazel will tell you what the month means before they tell you the price.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Guildmaster
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: They ran the guild hall for two terms and never once changed out of the coat they close the stall in. The committee took the minutes; Hazel took whatever the Capital City had thrown out.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Merchant
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Whenever you gain a non-Statue Market card, draw 1 card. Busy: look at the top two cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Half the borough calls the sky-reading patter. The other half has noticed that Hazel is packing up a stall of exactly the right stock three nights before anyone announces the sale.

cards.name: Hazel's Night Market
cards.text: Requires Hazel. Draw 2 cards, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The lamps go on, the trestles come out, and for six hours the town can buy anything at all. Hazel shakes on it before the other stallholders have finished counting.

cards.name: Hoot
cards.title: Night Porter
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. Busy: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: The knock comes at four. You did ask. Hoot has the list, your name is on it in a very neat hand, and Hoot has never once been late with one.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Bookmark Keeper
cards.text: When Inkwell is recruited, your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Four books open at once and a ribbon in each, and Inkwell can tell you what page every one of them is waiting on.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Storyteller
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. Busy: another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: The town under the lake, the doors in the hedge, the cousins of the moon. Nine listeners on the library floor, and every one of them up at dawn to go and look for one.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Night Librarian
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. When Inkwell becomes upright, nobody's Characters advance at the next Ready.
cards.flavor: The reading room goes quiet, the hall clock takes its time, and every animal who meant to leave an hour ago is still in their chair. Inkwell has not looked up.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Astronomer
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. When Inkwell completes a shift, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and at your rival's hand. Busy, once per game: Inkwell readies themselves.
cards.flavor: The Observatory steps, a flask, and a cat who is supposed to be asleep standing up as if the hour were a suggestion. They will tell you they were looking at Ursa; the other Mayor has stopped leaving their hand on the table.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Keeper of Stories
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. The first Event you play each turn that requires Lore lets you draw 1 card, and your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Ask whether any of it is true and you will be told, kindly and at length, that it is all research, and that the geography has never once contradicted itself, which is more than the borough's own history manages.

cards.name: Inkwell's Late Shift
cards.text: Requires Inkwell. Draw 3 cards, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: The candle burns down, the last of the little ones is carried home asleep, and Inkwell goes back to the chapter they were actually reading.

cards.name: Inkwell's Star Chart
cards.text: Requires Inkwell. Look at the top three cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Charted entirely from the good chair, which means half the sky is missing and the half that is there is right to the minute.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Messenger
cards.text: When you announce a purchase, look at the top 2 cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Every route in the borough in every weather there is, and not one delivery missed — though there is a note in the ledger about a cloudy Tuesday and a great deal of complaining.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Courier Captain
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. While Juniper is upright, your first bid each turn counts as 1 higher.
cards.flavor: They still run the fastest route in town. They simply have eleven other animals running it now, and an ephemeris on the wall of the sorting room.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Ward Councillor
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning.
cards.flavor: Four committees, two of them chaired, and not one animal on any of them could tell you the moment Juniper stopped being the one who brought the papers in.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Diplomat
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. Your opponent cannot raise a pending bid.
cards.flavor: They put it to each animal in the room in the way that animal needed to hear it, and by the time they had been round the table twice there was nothing left for anybody to raise.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Stargazer
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. At the start of your turn, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck; if you control another Science Character, gain 1 Supply as well.
cards.flavor: The Science hall finds it maddening and the Observatory finds it charming, and both have had to write down how often the call comes off. The post goes where it is addressed; the sky says when to set out.

cards.name: Kevin
cards.title: Hired Hand
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes back to the city after three of your turns. Each shift Kevin works pays 1 less than the last, down to 1. When Kevin is recruited, gain 1 Supply. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning.
cards.flavor: He said yes before you finished the sentence and he was at the yard before you were. Three. Then two. Then one, and a fox asleep on the sacks, and nobody in the borough has ever once been cross with him about it.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Night Printer
cards.text: When Lynnette is recruited, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply, or 2 less if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: Tomorrow's apprentice notices, printed tonight, free, whether or not anybody asked her for them.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Bookbinder
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. When Lynnette completes a shift, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply, or 2 less if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: She got the press cheap because it was broken and learned to mend it because nobody else would, and a mended spine has been her idea of a good evening ever since.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Lending Librarian
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. When Lynnette is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Thursday, on the floor, about nine rabbits and whoever else wandered in, all the voices done properly. One of them always comes back on the Friday asking how you get a job.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Master Printer
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. Your Master Characters are ready a turn sooner. Busy: draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The press runs all night and by morning the whole borough is reading the same page, which is why the animal who turns up on Tuesday to do the job already knows how the job is done.

cards.name: The All-Night Café
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Food Character, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Bean's, by the Hiring Hall, open when everything else is shut. Peanut keeps its books and works the day counter; Bean owns it and has never once been seen sitting down.

cards.name: The Festival Green
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: It was here before this Mayor and it will be here after, and on any given evening there is a band on it that nobody booked. Entertainment became a study because of what kept happening here after the shift ended.

cards.name: Hiring Hall
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Half its second chances were somebody else's first. An animal who has stopped getting up is sent to Rosabeth's gate, spends a season on the beds, and comes back through this door; and Biff has walked more animals up these steps than anyone has counted.

cards.name: Winter Stores
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: Whenever Supply is taken from you, take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: Copper drew up the list the borough works from — salt, lamp oil, candle stock — and then built the one thing his own cellar has never had: a door somebody else is allowed to open. He says the town's stores are for the town. His are for later.

cards.name: Fresh Batch
cards.text: Requires a Food Character. Gain 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Out of the oven at five, on the counter at six, gone by half past. Bean does not advertise it and has never needed to.

cards.name: Open Mic Night
cards.text: Requires an Entertainment Character. Draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Whatever room will have it, whoever turns up, four of Oatmeal's brothers and sisters at the back. The borough's evenings are not a rarity and never have been.

cards.name: Hedge Apothecary
cards.text: Requires a Hedgehog and a Mouse. Gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card, then you may rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Betty gathers it, loudly, with a charge if the ground is difficult. Rosabeth grinds it and sings over it. Neither will say which half is the part that works.

cards.name: Slack Water
cards.text: Requires an Otter and a Squirrel. Move a shift from one of your Characters to another, then gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Between tides there is a lull just long enough to hand the job to somebody else, and an otter who will take it off you before you have finished offering.

cards.name: Fair Hearing
cards.text: Requires two Civics Characters. Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for free and draw 2 cards. Your opponent gains 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Biff gives his account, which takes a while because he starts with everyone's names. Brett reads the clause. The animal in the dock walks out with a job, which is how it usually goes.

cards.name: Community Oven
cards.text: Gain 3 Supply, then ready one of your Food Characters.
cards.flavor: The borough's ovens are banked overnight and shared out by morning, which is the arrangement that made Food a study and not a sideline.

cards.name: The Bandstand
cards.text: Gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card, then ready one of your Entertainment Characters.
cards.flavor: Lanterns, a rail, and room for a band of five if two of them stand on the step. It was built for speeches and has never once been used for one.

cards.name: Emergency Reserve
cards.text: Put 3 Supply by on one of your Characters. Goes Out of Play.
cards.flavor: Salt, lamp oil, candle stock, and whatever coin is going spare this quarter. Copper will tell anyone who asks that it is nowhere near enough yet, and has been saying so for twenty years.

cards.name: The Tax Assessors
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 4 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: They come out from the Capital City with clipboards and nobody remembers inviting them. Copper has met them four times and has never once been surprised.

cards.name: Open Hiring Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor may rehire one Character from their Unemployment for free; it enters upright. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Trestle tables on the green and a queue that moves surprisingly fast, because half of it has already spent a season on Rosabeth's beds and is fit to be somewhere else.

cards.name: The Allotment Strip
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control an Agriculture Character, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Four generations of Clover's family have held this strip, and Clover is the first of them to write down what it does in a wet year.
cards.addedBecause: The strip is the Agriculture answer: land your own town works, against a Capital City that only ever sold you buildings. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: Copper's Cellar
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Under the weights office, stocked since he was an apprentice: salt, lamp oil, candle stock and a shelf of small coin. It was not opened the year the bridge went and it was not opened the winter the Grain Exchange shut — both times the salt went out on the quiet instead.
cards.addedBecause: Copper's cellar was the clearest thing in the bible that is a building and belongs to one town rather than to the Capital City. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: Berry's Bench
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Berry retired, and was back on the bench inside a fortnight. Whatever the borough breaks, it ends up here, and so does whoever broke it.
cards.addedBecause: The wake-up is the verb the remade Crafts cast leans on hardest, and nothing a town could build answered it. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: Rosabeth's Gate
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, your next rehire this turn costs 2 less.
cards.flavor: An animal who has lost a place and stopped getting up ends up at her gate, usually sent by somebody, and is put to work on the beds until they are fit to be somewhere else.
cards.addedBecause: Half the Hiring Hall's second chances start at this gate, so the town's own answer to Unemployment should be a thing a Mayor builds. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: The Open Mic Room
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control an Entertainment Character, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Whatever room will have them, a night a week, five in the band if two of them stand on the step. Oatmeal has never once cancelled.
cards.addedBecause: Entertainment had a Market card and an Event and nothing permanent; a study whose whole work is a room needed a room. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: The Boat Shed
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Down past the ferry steps, where the lightermen keep what the harbour office would rather not know about. Brooke has had a key for eight years.
cards.addedBecause: It pays on every shift the town works, which is the one thing a Capital City Building has never done. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: The Gate Hut
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, the next card revealed in the Capital City does not affect you.
cards.flavor: A bar, a lamp, and a hedgehog asleep behind both. The gate is shut from six and Bob does not care who you say you are.
cards.addedBecause: Bob keeps the county gate and the borough's weather comes through it; bracing against a shared shock is what a gate is for. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all, because the type did not exist when it was printed.

cards.name: Rabbit Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Rabbit token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Handed out at the warren door and counted back at the end of the evening, which is the only way anybody has ever established how many rabbits were actually there.
cards.addedBecause: Tokens are a new card type and neither shelf has one, so there is nothing to remake. The set declares one kind for every species, one for every field of study, and one for Buildings, so the first card that wants to count something a town already is does not have to invent a counter of its own.

cards.name: Mouse Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Mouse token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Rosabeth keeps hers in the tin the seed labels came in. Bella has never lost one and can tell you, unprompted, the week she was given each.

cards.flavor: Bob has four and has never once produced them at the gate, on the grounds that a hedgehog who needs a token to prove he is a hedgehog has bigger problems.

cards.text: An Otter token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Drilled through the middle so it can go on the line with the keys, which is Brooke’s doing: everything an otter owns has to survive being dropped in the water.

cards.flavor: Peanut has a great many and will not spend one, on the grounds that a rainy day is coming. Peanut is right about this roughly once every four years.

cards.flavor: Issued to every Cat in the borough. Inkwell’s has not been seen since the night it was issued and Inkwell is entirely unbothered about it.

cards.flavor: Collected at dusk rather than at the Hiring Hall’s hours, after Hoot pointed out mildly that every Owl in the borough was asleep at eleven in the morning.

cards.flavor: Finn can tell you what one is worth this week. Kevin has spent his, twice, and turned up cheerfully to ask whether there were any more.

cards.flavor: Hazel has a bag of them, and not one of the bag came from the Hiring Hall. Every single one was found, and every single one is genuine.

cards.flavor: Cut from the same board as the seed labels, and the first batch went out with Clover’s potato beds stamped on the back by mistake. Nobody has asked for the mistake to be corrected.

cards.flavor: Biff signs for his and for whoever he has walked up the Hiring Hall steps that week, which is why the Civics ledger never balances and has never once been queried.

cards.flavor: Copper weighed one, wrote the weight down, and weighs a fresh one every quarter to see whether the Capital City has started shaving them. It has not. He will keep checking.

cards.text: A Crafts token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Barrow’s has his thumbprint pressed into the soft side of it, put there the day the borough struck them, because a thing worth making is worth knowing who made it.

cards.text: A Lore token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Kept in the Lending Library’s long drawer with the ribbons. Lynnette prints the replacements, and the replacements are better than the originals, which Inkwell finds very funny.

cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Science token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Comet read the specification twice before collecting hers, in case she had misunderstood it the first time. She had not. She wanted to be sure.

cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Food token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Bean keeps the cafe’s in the till, under the tray, and Peanut counts them with the takings every night whether or not anybody has asked for a count.
cards.addedBecause: Tokens are a new card type and neither shelf has one, so there is nothing to remake. cards.name: Entertainment Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: An Entertainment token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Struck last of the eight, because Entertainment was the last study the borough admitted it had. Oatmeal was handed the first one on a stage, which is exactly where he would have chosen to be handed it.
cards.addedBecause: Tokens are a new card type and neither shelf has one, so there is nothing to remake. The set declares one kind for every species, one for every field of study, and one for Buildings, so the first card that wants to count something a town already is does not have to invent a counter of its own.

cards.name: Building Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Building token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: A surveyor’s chit, issued when a roof goes on and kept by the Mayor who raised it. Barrow has more of them than anyone in the borough and keeps them in the tin his father kept nails in.
cards.addedBecause: Tokens are a new card type and neither shelf has one, so there is nothing to remake. The set declares one kind for every species, one for every field of study, and one for Buildings, so the first card that wants to count something a town already is does not have to invent a counter of its own.

cards.name: Barrow's Measure
cards.text: Requires Barrow and a Crafts Character. Gain 2 Supply, and the next Building you buy costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: He walks the lot before the auction, on his own, and comes back with a figure. The Capital City has never yet asked less than the figure and has never once been more than a Supply above it.
cards.addedBecause: Barrow is the borough’s stonecutter and the only animal in the collection who moves a Building’s price; the printed set has no Event that does, because until `buildingDiscount` existed no card could.

cards.name: Biff's Beat
cards.text: Requires Biff. One of your opponent's Characters turns one step back toward Busy, then you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: The trouble stops, because Biff is immovable and it does. Then he walks them home, and a week later he has found them something to do. Both halves of that are the job; he has given up explaining which is the important one.
cards.addedBecause: Biff’s whole remake turns on `makeBusy` and nothing in the market answers it. The Event is the beat itself — stop the trouble, then find the animal a place — which no single card of his could hold on its own.

cards.name: Rosabeth's Rounds
cards.text: Requires Rosabeth and an Agriculture Character. Rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for free, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: She does the beds first and the borough second, and by the time she has got round to the second half of it somebody has been on the beds a fortnight and is fit to be somewhere else.
cards.addedBecause: The filtered `rehire` was built for Rosabeth’s gate and only one of her cards uses it; the Event is the gate itself, and Agriculture had no character-named Event of its own.

cards.name: Oatmeal's Benefit Night
cards.text: Requires Oatmeal and an Entertainment Character. Draw 2 cards and gain 2 Supply. Your opponent gains 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Whatever the hall takes goes to whoever needs it, and Oatmeal has never once checked which town they were from before handing it over. Four of his brothers and sisters at the back, as always.
cards.addedBecause: Entertainment has one Event and it names nobody; Oatmeal introduced the study and had none of his own. The Supply that crosses the table is the whole point of him and only an Event can say it.

cards.name: Copper's Stocktake
cards.text: Requires Copper and a Commerce Character. Look at the top three cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump, then gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Everything out, everything weighed, everything written down, and the half of it that was never going to be any use carried out to the yard. He does it twice a year and is cheerful for a week afterwards.
cards.addedBecause: The weights office is the borough’s idea of a clean ledger, and `scryDeck: { to: "dump" }` was built for an auditor — Barnaby’s — with no card of Copper’s using it.

cards.name: Warren Muster
cards.text: Requires two Rabbits. Recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Two rabbits is a conversation. Two rabbits and a notice on the Lending Library door is nine of them on the step by Thursday, and one of them already holding a tool.
cards.addedBecause: The Rabbit signature is `recruitFromHand` and every card that carries it is a Character; a species whose whole charter is arriving in crowds should have one Event that is the crowd arriving.

cards.name: The Night Round
cards.text: Requires two Owls. Two of your Characters each turn one step toward upright, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: Bean opens the counter, Hoot does the doors, Barnaby is already at the ledger. By the time the rest of the borough is up, the night has quietly put half of tomorrow in order.
cards.addedBecause: Owls own the night and the wake-up call, and the remade set gave them three characters and no Event at all — the one hour of the day when the borough’s Owls are all awake together had nothing to show for it.

cards.name: The Bins at Dawn
cards.text: Requires a Raccoon. Take a card from the City Dump, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Hazel is back before the lamps go out, with something the Capital City threw away and a straight face about where it came from. It is always exactly the thing the borough needed and nobody asks.
cards.addedBecause: Nobody but a Raccoon touches the City Dump, and `takeFromCityDump` appears on no Event on either shelf — the species signature had no card a whole town could play.

cards.name: Guild Night
cards.text: Requires two Crafts Characters. Ready one of your Characters and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The bench gets cleared, the good chairs come out, and whatever anyone is stuck on goes round the table once. Berry says nothing for an hour and then says the thing that fixes it.
cards.addedBecause: Crafts is the borough’s biggest study on the maker shelf and had no Event of its own; the guild evening is the one night the whole trade is in a room together.

cards.name: A Lecture at the Hall
cards.text: Requires two Science Characters. Draw 2 cards, and your next Event needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: Comet asks the question everyone else had decided not to ask, twice, and is not embarrassed either time. Half the hall leaves knowing something; the other half leaves knowing what to look up.
cards.addedBecause: Science arrived with the Night Shift and has no Event that asks for it by name. The lecture is the study doing what it is for — which is making the next thing cheaper to attempt.

cards.name: Ledger Day
cards.text: Requires two Commerce Characters. Gain 4 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Quarter day. Half the borough’s accounts pass over Peanut’s counter between orders, and everybody who comes in for a cup leaves knowing something they did not know about what things cost.
cards.addedBecause: Commerce is the study the remade cast is thickest in and the only Event naming it also names Peanut; the quarter’s books are the study’s own day and belong to nobody in particular.

cards.name: Barrow's Yard
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, the next Building you buy this turn costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Stone stacked by size, the good sand under a tarpaulin, and a Badger who will tell you what a wall is worth whether or not you have asked. He bids on every lot that comes up with a roof on it.
cards.addedBecause: A Mayor’s own yard is what makes the Capital City’s roofs affordable, and `buildingDiscount` was built for Barrow with exactly one card using it. And by construction: the printed set has no Town Buildings at all.

cards.name: The Warren
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Rabbit, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Nobody built it and nobody can say how far back it goes. Clover’s family came out of one end of it and Lynnette’s press sits over the other, and on any given morning there are more rabbits in it than were in it last night.
cards.addedBecause: Every Town Building so far answers a study; the borough’s species deserve the same, and Rabbits — whose whole charter is numbers — are where a building full of them says the most.

cards.name: The Observatory Steps
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Science Character, look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Inkwell swept them for a season to be allowed up them and Comet read every book at the top before the board would look at her. Whoever is on the steps at four in the morning knows what is coming before the borough does.
cards.addedBecause: The Observatory is in the town bible and in three backstories and was in nobody’s deck. Science had no permanent card of its own on either shelf.

cards.name: The Counting House
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, if you control a Commerce Character, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: A long desk, two lamps and the borough’s quarterly returns in order of age. Copper weighs what comes in and Peanut works out what it was worth, usually between orders and usually before being asked.
cards.addedBecause: Commerce is the study that turns other animals’ work into money, which is a thing a building does and not a thing a shift does. Nothing permanent on either shelf paid a Commerce town for the work of the rest of it.

cards.name: The Quill Wall
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your Characters cannot be targeted by your opponent until your next turn, and your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect this turn.
cards.flavor: Bob leans on it, Biff walks past it four times a night, and Berry mended the gate in it twice without being asked. It is not much of a wall. Nothing has ever got over it.
cards.addedBecause: Protection is the Hedgehog signature and it lives entirely on Characters; a town of them had nothing it could build. The borough has four Hedgehogs and this is the thing all four of them are.

cards.name: The Guild Hall
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Crafts Character, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The engine course runs here twice a year and Comet took it twice. Barrow will not join and turns up anyway, on the grounds that somebody has to tell them about foundations.
cards.addedBecause: The Capital City sells a Building for Food and one for Entertainment and none for the trade that builds them. Crafts is the maker shelf’s largest study and had nothing to buy.

cards.name: The Long Room
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Lore Character, look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Lending Library’s upper floor, where the ribbons live and the reading lamps are never all out. Inkwell has a chair in it that everybody knows is theirs and nobody has ever said so out loud.
cards.addedBecause: Lore is where the remade set does its looking and the Capital City sells it nothing; the Lending Library is in half the backstories on the shelf and was on no card at all.

newStudies.name: Food
newStudies.blurb: Feeding the town: counters, kitchens, carts and the café. Where Commerce counts the money and Agriculture grows the crop, Food is the animal who hands it over and knows everyone's order.
newStudies.note: A seventh study, declared on the maker shelf only. Before the maker set can be played, Food must be added to the printed set's `studies`, given a place in the species charters and deck tooling, and the printed decks re-checked — they were tuned against six.

newStudies.name: Entertainment
newStudies.blurb: The town's evenings: stages, bands, open mic nights, the halls people fill when the shift is over. Civics keeps the town working and Entertainment keeps it worth working for.
newStudies.note: An eighth study, declared on the maker shelf only. Like Food it must be added to the printed set's `studies`, given a place in the species charters and the deck tooling, and the printed decks re-checked before the maker set can be played.

townCards.note: The market side of the shelf: Buildings, Events, Market cards and Disruptions remade to give the remade cast, species and studies something to play with. Most carry `remakes` like any other maker card and are ticked off the same list; the Town Buildings carry `addition: true` and an `addedBecause` line instead, because the type did not exist in the printed set and there is nothing for them to replace, but they belong to no character entry — a Building is not somebody's backstory. The first batch exists mainly to give Food and Entertainment a market side at all: before it, neither new study had a single Building, Event, Market card or Disruption anywhere in the collection. Town Buildings have no art yet: `wantedArt` lists what each one should show, so the illustrations can be commissioned in one batch. A town card has no character entry to hang a wantedArt list on, which is why it lives here.

batches.why: Food and Entertainment had no market side; the rehire, discount and loss-recovery verbs the remade cast now leans on had nothing in the Capital City answering them.

batches.what: 7 Town Buildings (the first on either shelf)
batches.why: Town Buildings are a new card type and the printed set has none, so the maker shelf is where the type gets its first cards. They are the permanent half of a Mayor's own deck — a strip, a cellar, a bench, a gate — against the Capital City's civic monuments, and each one is a place the town bible already established. Every one is an addition: there is no printed Town Building to remake.

batches.what: 11 Events, 5 Town Buildings, 2 Capital City Buildings
batches.why: Support for particular characters, species and studies, which is what the market side was thinnest in. Barrow, Biff, Rosabeth, Oatmeal and Copper had no Event of their own; Rabbits, Owls and Raccoons had none that asked for the species; Crafts, Science and Commerce had none that asked for the study; and Crafts, Lore, Science, Commerce and the borough's four Hedgehogs had nothing permanent to build or buy. Several verbs built for the remakes — makeBusy, the filtered rehire, scryDeck to the Dump, buildingDiscount — were carried by one Character each and by nothing a whole town could play.

batches.what: 19 Tokens, the first on either shelf
batches.why: A new card type again, for the same reason as the Town Buildings: the printed set has none, so the maker shelf is where the type gets its first cards. What they are and why they exist before the cards that spend them is in the `tokens` block.

wantedArt.what: A long allotment strip in late summer, four generations of tools against the fence, one rabbit writing in a notebook at the end of it.
A cellar under a weights office: salt sacks, lamp oil, candle stock and a shelf of small coin, everything squared away and plainly never touched.
A tinkerer's workbench under a window, half the borough's broken things queued along it, two stools because somebody is always being taught.
A garden gate standing open onto raised beds, an animal being handed a trowel just inside it.
A back room set out with chairs, a band of five with two of them on the step, a lamp on the piano.
A boat shed past the ferry steps at dusk, lighters tied up, a lamp lit inside and the harbour office's windows dark.
A county gate barred for the night, a lamp on the post and a hedgehog asleep in the hut behind it.
A stonecutter's yard: stone stacked by size, the good sand under a tarpaulin, a Badger with a rule in his paw looking at a lot over the fence.
A hillside with a dozen doors in it at dusk and a printing shed built over one end, more rabbits arriving than leaving.
Long stone steps up to an observatory door at four in the morning, a lamp at the top, a swept broom left against the rail.
A long desk under two lamps, the borough's quarterly returns stacked in order of age, scales at one end and a coffee cup at the other.
A low wall at night with a hedgehog leaning on it and a lamp beyond. Nothing dramatic, and nothing getting over it.
A trade hall mid-lesson: an engine in pieces on the floor, the benches full, a Badger at the back with his arms folded.
The Lending Library's upper floor: ribbons in a long drawer, the reading lamps still lit, one chair that is plainly somebody's.

tokens.note: The token shelf. A token is a marker a Mayor holds beside their Supply — never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck — and each kind is declared by one card here: ten species, eight studies, and one for Buildings. The rules are spec/game.json `tokens`; the engine holds the counts in `player.tokens` and gives, spends and reads them with `gainToken`, `spendToken` and the `tokensAtLeast` condition. Nothing on either shelf spends one yet, and that is deliberate. Tokens are the obvious answer to a whole family of cards the collection keeps reaching for — 'your Rabbits are worth something to each other', 'Food pays for Food', 'the town has built before and it shows' — and every one of those cards wants the same counter underneath it. Building the counter once, before any of them exist, is what stops the first three of them each inventing their own.

wantedArt.what: One sheet of ten round wooden chits, each stamped with a species in the borough's own hand — not a portrait but a maker's mark: ears, a tail, a set of quills. Worn edges; these have been in pockets.
One sheet of eight square chits carrying the study icons already used on the card faces, struck in the same wood and the same hand as the species sheet.
A single surveyor's chit, larger than the rest and stamped with a roofline, lying on the corner of a plan with a tin of them behind it.
